analysis: The PR only edits docs/reference/configuration.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one table row after line 323, `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED`. This is a documentation-only change to an engine/kernel-selection variable. The row says it selects the Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel for qwen3_5 models, with a probe default that keeps the four-row kernel only where it reproduces the stock kernel `gated_delta_step` bit for bit. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the row is unseen. The excerpt shows no shipped code, no new network or trust boundary, no key or attestation handling, no LaunchAgent passthrough change and no cache-format change. I saw nothing that touches the threat model's assets (A-001 through A-017) or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-010 and TB-011). The retained T-041 text covers prefix-cache storage, TTL, lookup-tag and AAD controls, and this documentation change does not alter any of them. Remaining uncertainty: the underlying kernel change in libs/mlx-swift-lm GatedDelta.swift is outside the supplied evidence. Whether the probe actually preserves bit-exact numerics, and whether it affects the correctness of the MLX path (T-007 and T-027 context), cannot be judged from this doc diff. The doc also does not state whether the variable is forwarded to the LaunchAgent, which is the portion of the row that was cut off. A later pass should check that code change and confirm the variable is not in `LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment`. That check is an integration question about unseen code, not evidence of a regression here.
